title: Peter Hoskin
gist: A Prospect contributor index page for books and culture editor Peter Hoskin, who is also the Daily Mail's games critic; his 50 listed pieces cluster on the video-games industry's troubles, prediction markets (“Polymarket is America, America is Polymarket”) and the philosophy of games.

insights.claim: Prospect's games coverage argues the most successful form of entertainment is failing and that “the future of games could kill the future of games”, alongside a piece on industry job cuts titled “Swinging the axe”.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Sustained editorial focus on layoffs and structural decline in the largest entertainment category — a negative read-through for games publishers and studios.
insights.quote: The most successful form of entertainment is failing

insights.claim: Prediction markets are treated as a defining American cultural phenomenon rather than a niche financial product, in a piece titled “Polymarket is America, America is Polymarket”.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Mainstream cultural framing of prediction markets tends to precede retail adoption and regulatory attention.
insights.quote: Polymarket is America, America is Polymarket

insights.claim: The beat pairs games criticism with philosophy-of-games thinking, including an interview with C Thi Nguyen under the heading “All a game”, suggesting games are being used as a general framework for analysing incentives and agency.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Game-theoretic and gamification framings of markets and politics are entering mainstream commentary.
insights.locator: C Thi Nguyen: All a game
